messages.author: 25f4eac5601628b9
messages.subject: Warning message and only standardized solution for CFA
parts:
Hello All,

I am trying to do a CFA with 1 factor and 10 items. But I get the following message and only the standardized loadings are available:

Warning message:
In lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable, :
lavaan WARNING: the optimizer (NLMINB) claimed the model converged,
but not all elements of the gradient are (near) zero;
the optimizer may not have found a local solution
use check.gradient = FALSE to skip this check.

Thank you for your help.

Katalin

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Warning message and only standardized solution for CFA
parts:
The message is probably giving you the straight answer--the algorithm may have settled on a local optimum rather than on a global optimum, so you perhaps should not trust the solution. Do the estimates look odd?
You might (a) re-run the analysis with specified starting values. You could use syntax like:

factor1 =~ 0.7?y1 + 0.7?y2 etc.

to suggest starting values of 0.7 for those two loadings. Suggest plausible starting values and see if the algorithm converges to a plausible solution.

Or you might (b) re-run the analysis while excluding some of your observed variables--maybe half of them. If the full model is correct in the population, the estimates with the half-model should be approximately the same, but you will have a better chance of convergence. This may also suggest better starting values for strategy (a), above.
     You have not said anything about your data, so for the moment I will assume that there are no problems there.

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Warning message and only standardized solution for CFA
parts:
Katalin,

Loadings are the rare case where you should focus on standardized coefficients. Also, can you share your function call? cfa(), or whichever you used?

I would also take a random 5, not the first 5 for Ed's suggestion. Looking at the R^2 in the first output, you're over-representing variables with the lowest R^2.

Finally, N=148 isn't very many for a CFA, perhaps especially with 10 items, and definitely not very many for an EFA. I don't suggest splitting your sample.

Pat

Notice the R2 for the first indicator is very low. This is the indicator which lavaan chooses, by default, to get a loading fixed to 1. It can be a problem when this "reference indicator" is weak. But you could easily change this. The program goes with the first indicator mentioned in your syntax. Task9 appears to be your strongest indicator. In your syntax, just move Task9 to the front of the line of syntax (next to the =~ operator) so that Task9 becomes the reference indicator.
--Ed Rigdon
On Tue, Dec 29, 2020 at 11:17 AM Katalin Grajzel <kati...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thanks for the quick answer. Now that you have pointed out the loadings and variances are all off. The data is fine. I am assuming the loadings are off because of the warning. When I split my 296 data points the loadings look a lot better but they are still very high. EFA looks good and suggest one factor. Not sure why CFA is not converging. 
I am not sure about staring values as this is a novel examination and there has not been any published articles on this. 
Any suggestions?

On Dec 29, 2020, at 8:57 AM, Edward Rigdon <edward...@gmail.com> wrote:

The message is probably giving you the straight answer--the algorithm may have settled on a local optimum rather than on a global optimum, so you perhaps should not trust the solution. Do the estimates look odd?
You might (a) re-run the analysis with specified starting values. You could use syntax like:

factor1 =~ 0.7?y1 + 0.7?y2 etc.

to suggest starting values of 0.7 for those two loadings. Suggest plausible starting values and see if the algorithm converges to a plausible solution.

Or you might (b) re-run the analysis while excluding some of your observed variables--maybe half of them. If the full model is correct in the population, the estimates with the half-model should be approximately the same, but you will have a better chance of convergence. This may also suggest better starting values for strategy (a), above.
     You have not said anything about your data, so for the moment I will assume that there are no problems there.

                  the optimizer may not have found a local solution
                  use check.gradient = FALSE to skip this check.

Thank you for your help.

Katalin
